html:
The blues is a music that grew among African Americans in the Deep South around 1900, above all in the Mississippi Delta. It drew on work songs, field hollers and spirituals, with bent "blue" notes and a pattern of twelve bars.

W. C. Handy published blues songs from 1912, and in 1920 Mamie Smith made the first blues record by a Black singer, a hit. Delta players such as Charley Patton and Robert Johnson sang of hard times, love and travel with a guitar.

In the Great Migration musicians such as Muddy Waters took it north to Chicago and electrified it. The blues fed jazz and became the basis of rock and roll, and through the Rolling Stones and others it shaped music worldwide.
